series_items.subject: [PATCH 1/2] mm: refactor find_next_best_node to find_next_best_node_in
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the find_next_best_node() function to find_next_best_node_in(), which takes an explicit candidates nodemask instead of relying on N_MEMORY. This change enables building fallback lists with non-N_MEMORY candidates, but does not introduce any functional changes as callers still select from N_MEMORY. The refactor affects three files: mm/internal.h, mm/memory-tiers.c, and mm/page_alloc.c.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/2] mm/page_alloc: refactor build_node_zonelist() out of build_zonelists()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the build_zonelists() function in the Linux kernel's page allocation module to extract a new function, build_node_zonelist(), which constructs per-node fallback lists from candidate nodemasks. This change allows for building new zonelists based on node masks instead of just using the default N_MEMORY node state list. The patch does not introduce any functional changes and maintains the same behavior as before.

review_comments.author: Vlastimil (SUSE)
review_comments.summary: Reviewer suggested moving pr_cont() printing into build_node_zonelist() and eliminating the node_order array, which would require modifying build_zonelists_in_node_order() to process nodes piece-meal
review_comments.raw_body:
LGTM, but, while we're at it, could we just do the pr_cont() printing in
build_node_zonelist() itself (maybe behind a flag if you don't want to print
from future new caller) so it doesn't need to pass nr_nodes back to
build_zonelists(). Then also the node_order array could live in
build_node_zonelist() itself?

Actually I wonder if we could get ride of the node_order array completely.
It would mean the loop processing in build_zonelists_in_node_order() would
have to be done piece-meal in build_node_zonelist() itself. But seems
feasible? Depends on how you intend to reuse/extend the new functions later,
I guess...

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch refactors the zonelist constructors and iterators in the Linux kernel to make them more flexible and modular. The changes include extracting a new function `find_next_best_node_in` that takes an explicit candidate set, and moving the per-node construction loop out of `build_zonelists` into a separate function `build_node_zonelist`. These changes allow for building zonelists over custom sets of nodes and iterating over them in fallback order. The refactoring is intended to be functional equivalent to the original code, but with improved modularity and flexibility.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] fs: stamp the current time for a stale delegated ctime update
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a timing issue in inode_set_ctime_deleg() where an update that doesn't advance the ctime is skipped, but should instead record the current time to maintain visibility of delegated changes. The patch modifies the function to stamp the current time when the update does not advance the ctime.

review_comments.author: Jan Kara
review_comments.summary: Identified the correct behavior for inode_set_ctime_deleg() when an update does not advance the ctime, and approved the patch as it correctly stamps the current time in such cases.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Wed 02-09-26 14:54:14, Jeff Layton wrote:
> inode_set_ctime_deleg() drops an update that does not advance the ctime.
> That is correct when a client reports a timestamp that it advanced on its
> own. It is wrong when the client moves the timestamp backwards on purpose,
> as utimensat() does.
> 
> Stamp the current time in that case. The ctime still never moves backwards.
> 
> Fixes: 3952f1cbcbc4 ("nfsd: fix SETATTR updates for delegated timestamps")
> Assisted-by: LLM
> Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

Looks good to me. Feel free to add:

Reviewed-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>

								Honza

> ---
>  fs/inode.c | 17 +++++++++++++----
>  1 file changed, 13 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
> 
> diff --git a/fs/inode.c b/fs/inode.c
> index ba7da39be4a3..8391814a4016 100644
> --- a/fs/inode.c
> +++ b/fs/inode.c
> @@ -2959,11 +2959,17 @@ EXPORT_SYMBOL(inode_set_ctime_current);
>   * inode attributes, including the mtime. When updating the mtime, update
>   * the ctime to a value at least equal to that.
>   *
> - * This can race with concurrent updates to the inode, in which
> - * case the update is skipped.
> + * The ctime never moves backwards. An @update that does not advance the ctime
> + * records the current time instead, so that the delegated change is still
> + * visible in the ctime.
> + *
> + * This can still race with a concurrent update to the inode. That stamp takes
> + * precedence, and is at least as recent as the one it displaces.
>   *
>   * Note that this works even when multigrain timestamps are not enabled,
>   * so it is used in either case.
> + *
> + * Returns the resulting ctime.
>   */
>  struct timespec64 inode_set_ctime_deleg(struct inode *inode, struct timespec64 update)
>  {
> @@ -2975,9 +2981,12 @@ struct timespec64 inode_set_ctime_deleg(struct inode *inode, struct timespec64 u
>  	cur_ts.tv_nsec = cur & ~I_CTIME_QUERIED;
>  	cur_ts.tv_sec = inode_get_ctime_sec(inode);
>  
> -	/* If the update is older than the existing value, skip it. */
> +	/*
> +	 * The update does not advance the ctime. Stamp the current time, so
> +	 * that the delegated change is still visible in the ctime.
> +	 */
>  	if (timespec64_compare(&update, &cur_ts) <= 0)
> -		return cur_ts;
> +		return inode_set_ctime_current(inode);
>  
>  	ktime_get_coarse_real_ts64_mg(&now);
>  
> 
> -- 
> 2.55.0
> 
-- 
Jan Kara <jack@suse.com>
SUSE Labs, CR

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/3] nfsd: accept a backdated timestamp from a delegation holder
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows the NFS server to accept a backdated timestamp from a delegation holder, which was previously ignored if it moved backwards in time. The client can report file times at every delegation return, and the server will update them accordingly. If an mtime moves backwards, the ctime is set to the current time. The patch also fixes issues with caching and attribute updates when using delegations.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/3] nfsd: compare CB_GETATTR times against the inode
series_items.patch_summary: This patch updates the NFS server to compare client-reported timestamps in CB_GETATTR requests against the current timestamp of the inode, rather than stale values stored in the delegation. This change prevents clients from reporting outdated timestamps and ensures that file metadata is accurately updated. The patch also removes unnecessary fields from the delegation structure and fixes a bug related to SETATTR updates for delegated timestamps.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue where applications cannot set backdated timestamps on files due to strict attribute delegation rules in NFS. The patches modify the server-side code to accept these updates by changing how the ctime is handled, allowing for improved performance in common use-cases.

review_comments.author: Chuck Lever
review_comments.summary: Acknowledged the patches and suggested that Christian will want to take them through the VFS tree. Provided an Acked-by tag.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Wed, Sep 2, 2026, at 2:54 PM, Jeff Layton wrote:
> The main problem is that an attribute delegation has strict rules about
> updates can be done, and that prevents applications that backdate
> timestamps on files after writing them, (e.g. tar -x, cp -p, etc.) from
> setting them properly.
>
> We could fix this on the client by making it always issue an RPC for the
> SETATTR, but that would harm performance in these common use-cases.
> This set allows the server to accept some of these backdated mtime
> updates, by changing how the ctime is handled.
>
> It'd be nice to see this in v7.4.
>
> Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
> ---
> Changes in v2:
> - Split the change into three patches
> - Stamp now in inode_set_ctime_deleg() for a stale update, so nfsd need
>   not compare
> - Drop a SETATTR report that matches the inode, so an untouched file
>   keeps its change attribute
> - Set dl_setattr only on the branch that carries a c/mtime update
> - Compare against the inode, not the grant-time snapshots (Chuck)
> - Set the ctime whenever a CB_GETATTR moves the mtime
> - Take i_rwsem before the CB_GETATTR comparison
> - Drop the unused dl_atime, dl_mtime and dl_ctime, and make
>   nfsd4_vet_deleg_time() static
> - Link to v1: 
> https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260901-delegts-v1-1-9937f7ee4370@kernel.org
>
> ---
> Jeff Layton (3):
>       fs: stamp the current time for a stale delegated ctime update
>       nfsd: accept a backdated timestamp from a delegation holder
>       nfsd: compare CB_GETATTR times against the inode
>
>  fs/inode.c          | 17 +++++++++++----
>  fs/nfsd/nfs4proc.c  | 63 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++----------
>  fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c | 49 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++---------------
>  fs/nfsd/state.h     |  8 -------
>  4 files changed, 95 insertions(+), 42 deletions(-)
> ---
> base-commit: ac579868af0c900d8fd9c8cfe9e10db46ccc5a75
> change-id: 20260901-delegts-e91a648f1427
>
> Best regards,
> -- 
> Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

Since the series modifies fs/inode.c, Christian will want to take it
through the VFS tree.

Acked-by: Chuck Lever <cel@kernel.org>


-- 
Chuck Lever (Come to NFS bake-a-thon! https://nfsv4bat.org)
